root_cause: The merge-queue run was blocked by the Samples job, which runs tests/samples_tests/smoke_tests/test_benchmark_app.py::test_benchmark_app_sub_ms_console_output_only[True-C++] on a shared Windows CI runner. This test asserts the average benchmark_app latency stays below a fixed 1.0ms threshold to validate sub-millisecond console/JSON output formatting, but the actual measured average latency was 1.771ms. Since the PR under test (#39524) only touches src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/plugin/transformations_pipeline.cpp (a GPU-plugin transformation unrelated to CPU benchmark_app timing), and the test is run under pytest-xdist with 4 parallel workers (gw0-gw3) competing for CPU resources on the same runner, the most likely cause is transient CPU contention/noise on the Windows build-and-test runner inflating the measured single-inference latency above the hard 1.0ms bound rather than a real performance regression. Separately, the non-blocking 'Build (C++20, non-blocking)' job failed with the already-known, already-tracked GGUF frontend C++20 unicode build issue (pattern 60c87e1ef4d6a044); this job is not listed in Overall_Status's needs dependency chain and therefore did not itself cause the merge-queue block, but it is recorded here as a secondary observed failure of this run.
reproduction_steps: On a Windows runner with OpenVINO built and samples installed, run: python3 -bb -W error -X dev -X warn_default_encoding -m pytest ./tests/smoke_tests/test_benchmark_app.py::test_benchmark_app_sub_ms_console_output_only -k 'True and C++' --numprocesses auto. The failure is timing-dependent and may not reproduce on a quieter/faster machine; a tighter threshold or isolated (non-parallel) CPU affinity run is likely needed to reproduce reliably.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed Samples job; if CPU contention under pytest-xdist is the cause, a retry on a less-loaded runner should pass.

Consider loosening the 1.0ms threshold in test_benchmark_app_sub_ms_console_output_only or adding a retry/average-of-N-runs strategy to tolerate normal CI timing jitter (see tests/samples_tests/smoke_tests/test_benchmark_app.py:526).
Consider running this specific latency-sensitive test with reduced parallelism (e.g., pinned to a dedicated worker) instead of under pytest-xdist 'auto' parallel workers to avoid CPU contention.
Separately track/fix the non-blocking GGUF C++20 build failure (src/frontends/gguf/tests/test_parser.cpp:731) per existing pattern 60c87e1ef4d6a044 — unrelated to this PR and already non-blocking.
prevention_strategies: For latency-threshold-based smoke tests running under parallel test execution, prefer wider tolerance margins, warm-up iterations, or statistical comparisons (e.g., median of multiple runs) instead of a single hard millisecond cutoff, since parallel pytest-xdist workers sharing CPU cores on a Windows CI runner can transiently inflate per-inference latency well above a tight threshold with no underlying code regression.
